newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London sharply lower on dollar fall.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London sharply lower on dollar fall.

text.p: U.S. shares were sharply lower in London as falls in the dollar pressured stocks despite Wall Street's surge overnight, traders said.

The dollar slide began after a Japanese finance ministry official said the dollar's recovery from last year's post-war low against the yen was nearly complete. The comments raised fears that the G3 strong-dollar policy was under threat.
U.S. Treasuries also dropped, losing nearly half a point from New York's finish before stabilizing in London.
"Bonds and the dollar have led us down across the board," said one London trader.
"We're looking at a lower opening on Wall Street - maybe 20 points or so."
The only stock to buck the weaker trend was Intel, which rose 5/8 to 119-1/2.
Intel said yesterday it expected fourth-quarter revenues to be "significantly" higher than third quarter sales.

In New York, the Dow soared over 96 points - 1.59 percent - to record its first ever close above 6,100. It finished at 6,178 its biggest single day gain since March, after hectic buying in sectors seen benefiting from the U.S. election results.
